title: Remove SUSPENDED NFs from NRF registry
author: arora
rationale: NFs whose heartbeats stopped (status SUSPENDED) are kept in the NRF registry and still returned by NF discovery (UPF discovery output shown), so consumers can select dead instances; labelled Bug+Feature, closed by NRF MR !56. Peer failure inferred from SUSPENDED status; no error reaches the operator.

title: NRF crashing something when host is too stressed
author: defosseu
rationale: NRF assertion (in heartbeat-timeout handler) when all NFs register concurrently at start-up on a stressed host; not reproducible, closed 'not valid anymore'; trigger is a start-up burst, not a failure.

title: Deploying OAI Core Network Functions without any order (Only for service based architecture)
author: arora
rationale: Feature request to deploy NFs without start order; also notes that on NF restart the NRF keeps the old registration and AUSF/UDM keep stale peer IPs (new pod IPs). Restart-related stale state but framed as a deployment feature; closed 'fixed in develop'.

title: [Issue] SMF can't re-register to NRF if registration/heartbeat lost e.g., when NRF restarts

rationale: Title states the SMF cannot re-register with the NRF once registration/heartbeat is lost, e.g. when the NRF restarts (body empty; fixed by MR !263). After NRF restart the SMF stays undiscoverable, so procedures needing it fail. Labels inferred from title + fix note only.

title: SMF should re-register in case it receives 404 from NRF
